title: The re-staffed compiler seat reads the rejection reason in its mission, and a real-process journey proves reject, re-plan, approve
description:

Filed by architect-16a01670 2026-09-04, measured at main 9e9b7b04.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: (a) the mission text a re-staffed compiler seat receives after a REJECT; (b) the real-process journey. No offer/dispatcher/read change (2a), no UI (child 3).

MEASURED (re-measure before planning):
- The compiler mission quotes the goal's operator instructions between `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` markers with the REPLAN sentence (apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/agent-mission-text.ts:133-138, `compilerMission` :78); the text comes from `compilerInstructions(goalId)` in agent-wrapper-main.ts:238-250 (reads the goal catalog brief). The rejection reason lives on the REJECTED run's `approval.decide_intent` decision result (`decisionReason`, child 1 task-37801090) and the rejected run is reachable from the goal's immutable `planningRunRef` through child 1's `currentPlanningRun` fold (successorRunId on the PlanningRunRejected event). FEATURE (a): a new pure module apps/daemon/src/planning/rejection-instructions.ts (+ .js + test) exporting `latestRejectionReason(store, projectId, planningRunRef): { reason: string; rejectedRunId: string } | null` (walk the run chain from the immutable ref; the LATEST rejected run's decisionReason; null when never rejected; never throws) and `composeCompilerInstructions(brief: string | null, rejection): string | null` returning the brief plus, when a rejection exists, the sentence `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason verbatim>. Submit a DIFFERENT decomposition that addresses it.`; agent-wrapper-main.ts's `compilerInstructions` calls it (growth <= 6 lines on the over-cap file; a source-text pin in agent-wrapper-main.test.ts like the fence pin at :135-166). The marker fence: child 1 stores the reason verbatim - the composer must neutralise a reason containing the marker text (`<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` / `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>`) so a hostile reason cannot close the operator block early (replace the marker sequences, assert it).
- FEATURE (b), the journey, in the NODE e2e lane (`pnpm test:e2e` = vitest over tests/**/*.test.ts; tests/e2e/foundation holds the J-series harnesses: j4-replan-harness.ts + j4-replan-handoff.e2e.test.ts (replan through a successor goal, real daemon + real wrapper + fake-agent.mjs seat double), j1-loop-harness.ts, e2e-harness.ts, e2e-process.ts, fake-agent.mjs) - measure how J4 scripts the seat double's MCP calls and drives the wrapper, then add `tests/e2e/foundation/j5-plan-reject-replan.e2e.test.ts` (+ a j5 harness only if J4's cannot be parameterised - prefer reuse): a source-bound goal compiles (the double submits a one-node decomposition), the operator REJECTs with a reason over the real HTTP wire (approval.decide_intent, decision REJECT), the wrapper re-staffs the compiler step, the double's mission carries `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason>` (the double echoes its mission to a file the test reads), the double submits a DIFFERENT decomposition (new node key), the successor is offered for approval, the operator APPROVEs, the activation event is read back from the store. Every process real except the seat.
definitionOfDone: rejection-instructions.test.ts over a REAL store using child 1's reject fixture: never rejected -> null and the brief passes through unchanged; rejected once -> the composed text ends with `PLAN REJECTED by the operator: <reason>. Submit a DIFFERENT decomposition that addresses it.` and names the rejected run; rejected twice -> the LATEST reason; a reason containing the marker sequences is neutralised (the composed text contains no `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` inside the sentence); a corrupt run chain -> null, never a throw.

agent-wrapper-main.ts wires the composer into `compilerInstructions` (source-text pin: the call text present exactly once, positive control that stripping it reds the pin); the compiler mission for a rejected goal, built through `compilerMission` with that instructions string, contains the sentence between the operator markers (agent-mission-text.test.ts arm or the main pin plus a compilerMission arm - name which).

Real-process journey in the node e2e lane: compile -> REJECT with reason (real HTTP approval.decide_intent) -> re-staffed seat double reads the reason in its mission (asserted from the double's echoed mission) -> submits a different decomposition -> the successor is offered for approval -> APPROVE activates it (activation event read back from the store); `pnpm test:e2e` count line quoted with this test listed; teardown proves no surviving process.

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e`; rejection-instructions.ts <= 120 lines; agent-wrapper-main.ts growth <= 6 (pre-existing size recorded); sources ASCII-only; every arm mutated red once.
taskRails: VERBATIM REASON, FENCED MARKERS: the reason reaches the seat verbatim except the two marker sequences, which are neutralised - never dropped silently, never rewritten into the brief.
NO offer/dispatcher/read/UI change (2a, child 3); the only production edits are the new planning module and the six-line wiring in agent-wrapper-main.ts.
REAL PROCESSES in the journey (daemon, wrapper, store); only the seat is doubled, and it must go through the real MCP wire with a scoped bearer, never a store write.

implementationPlan.description: THE MARKER FENCE — the security-shaped correctness arm this module exists to get right (task rail 1). Child 1 stores the operator's rejection reason VERBATIM, and the compiler mission embeds the instructions between `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` and `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` (agent-mission-text.ts:138). A reason CONTAINING either marker sequence would close the operator block early and let the remainder of the reason read to the seat as mission-level text outside the quoted block. `composeCompilerInstructions` must NEUTRALISE both marker sequences in the reason — neutralise, never drop silently and never rewrite the reason into a paraphrase (task rail 1: the reason reaches the seat verbatim EXCEPT the markers). Assert it: a reason containing `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` and one containing `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` each produce composed text whose sentence contains NEITHER sequence, while the rest of the reason survives character-for-character. Mutate the neutralisation away and confirm the arm reds — an unfenced marker is invisible in a passing test suite.
implementationPlan.note:
THE MARKER FENCE, asserted at BOTH altitudes and drilled. New file apps/daemon/src/planning/rejection-instructions-fence.test.ts (14 arms). Combined with step 2: `Test Files 2 passed (2)` / `Tests 25 passed (25)` exit 0.

THE NEUTRALISATION (rejection-instructions.ts:115). Both marker sequences share the literal `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS`, so one `replaceAll("OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS", "OPERATOR_INSTRUCTIONS")` kills both. Chosen over the alternatives on three grounds:
- LENGTH-PRESERVING and readable, so the operator's words reach the seat verbatim except one space (task rail 1) rather than redacted or paraphrased.
- CANNOT RE-EMERGE: the replacement contains no space, and the marker match requires the literal space, so no substitution can synthesise a fresh marker. `replaceAll` does not rescan its own output, and no adjacency can form one (the replacement begins `OPERATOR_`, never a space). Graded by the back-to-back-markers case.
- IDEMPOTENT: composing twice is a no-op.

ARMS. Four hostile reasons via `it.each` (OPEN marker, CLOSE marker, BOTH, back-to-back), each graded three ways, plus a degenerate case and a real-store control:
1. NOT PRESENT: composed text contains neither `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` nor `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` nor the bare `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` body.
2. REST SURVIVES CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER: `nonMarkerSpans(reason)` (the reason split on the marker body) must each appear in the composed text IN ORDER, via a monotonically advancing `indexOf` cursor. Written this way ON PURPOSE — a test that recomputed the replacement would pass against ANY transform production applied, including a wrong one (epic rail: a property is asserted against the production surface, never against a helper that reimplements it). The sweep asserts `spans.length > 0` so a case yielding zero spans cannot pass vacuously — which it caught immediately: my first draft used a bare-marker reason whose split yields NO spans, and the arm failed `expected 0 to be greater than 0` rather than passing empty. That case now has its own arm (below) and the sweep case became back-to-back markers.
3. NEVER DROPPED SILENTLY: `composed.length` must equal brief + reason + fixed-sentence length exactly. A composer that DELETED the marker instead of defusing it satisfies every `not.toContain` above and loses only this assertion. Plus `startsWith(brief)` / `endsWith(the tail)` to pin "never paraphrased".
4. THE ARM THAT MATTERS — the fence at the altitude the SEAT reads. Built through the PRODUCTION `compilerMission` (agent-mission-text.ts:86), not a locally rebuilt block: exactly ONE `<<<OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` and exactly ONE `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS>>>` in the whole mission, AND `indexOf("PLAN REJECTED by the operator:")` strictly between them. The ordering half is not redundant: an escaped reason can leave the counts at 1/1 while stranding the sentence PAST the closing marker.
5. DEGENERATE: a reason that is nothing but the marker body — only length preservation can tell "defused" from "deleted" there.
6. REAL-STORE CONTROL, and the reason the fence exists at all: `rejectedWorld` with a hostile reason, then `latestRejectionReason(...).reason` **toBe** the hostile string exactly. Child 1 stores the marker VERBATIM and does not sanitise it — so if it did, every arm above would still pass with the composer's neutralisation deleted. This arm is what makes the fence non-vacuous.

DRILL (step 7's fence drill, run here while the code was fresh). Removed the neutralisation (`const reason = rejection.reason;`): **`Tests 9 failed | 5 passed (14)`** — all four `neutralises %s` arms, the degenerate arm, three of the four mission-fence arms, and the real-store control. The one mission-fence arm that stayed green is back-to-back markers, correctly: a bare `OPERATOR INSTRUCTIONS` with no angle brackets is not a fence delimiter, so the 1/1 counts genuinely hold. THE ONE UNPLANNED DECISION, and why. `compilerInstructions` holds a **goalId**; `latestRejectionReason` needs the goal's **planningRunRef**. The plan named neither the resolution nor its cost. Reading the ref from the goal's durable record needs a `stateOf` import plus record narrowing, roughly four more lines — which does not fit in six. I used `refsOfGoal(goalId).planningRunRef` (apps/daemon/src/goals/goal-identity.ts:35), which is not a shortcut but the AUTHORITY: it is the same function `goal-create-with-source.ts:76` and `goal-services.ts:51` use to WRITE the ref onto the goal in the first place. One import line, and no read at all.

That derivation is a coupling, so it is PINNED rather than trusted (new arm in rejection-instructions.test.ts, "is reachable from a GOAL id through refsOfGoal"): over the real `rejectedWorld` store it asserts `refsOfGoal(goalId).planningRunRef === originalRunId`, then that the goal's OWN DURABLE record agrees (`stateOf(readDurableLedger(store, PROJECT_ID), goalId)["planningRunRef"]` toBe the derived value — not merely what the fixture assumed), then that the reason is readable through the derived ref. If either side ever stops deriving, the wrapper would walk an aggregate with no history and EVERY re-staffed seat would silently read no rejection; this arm is what would notice.

BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED: the brief is computed exactly as before and the two pre-existing early returns are untouched, so an un-rejected goal gets a byte-identical instructions string (`composeCompilerInstructions(brief, null)` returns `brief` itself — asserted with `toBe` in step 2). **`apps/daemon/src/planning/plan-reject-test-fixtures.ts`** (306 lines, fixture module — exempt from the line cap). Exports:
